# aria_secret (Resource)

Secret resource
The platform never returns the value of a secret, and Terraform does not store it either (write-only attribute, requires Terraform 1.11 or later).
The provider detects a changed `value` through `value_checksum`, and a secret modified outside of Terraform through `updated_at`: in both cases the next plan proposes to overwrite the secret with your configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "database_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "aria_secret" "example" {
  name        = "DATABASE_PASSWORD"
  description = "Password of the application's database user"
  org_scoped  = true

  # Write-only, Terraform never stores it. Changing it updates the secret.
  value = var.database_password
}

resource "aria_secret" "project_example" {
  name        = "PROJECT_TOKEN"
  org_scoped  = false
  project_ids = ["56ff588e-31ca-4878-883f-b74f28fa27b8"]
  value       = var.database_password
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `name` (String) Secret name
- `value` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Secret value (write-only, never stored in the plan or the state).
Changing it updates the secret, see `value_checksum`.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Describe the resource in few sentences
- `org_scoped` (Boolean) Scoped to the organization?
Either this or `project_ids` must be set.
Default value is false.
- `project_ids` (Set of String) Restrict to given projects (an empty set means none)

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation date-time
- `created_by` (String) User who performed this action
- `id` (String) Identifier
- `org_id` (String) Organization identifier
- `updated_at` (String) Changed date-time
A value different from the one stored after the last apply means the secret was modified outside of Terraform, the next plan proposes to overwrite it.
- `updated_by` (String) User who performed this action
- `value_checksum` (String) SHA-256 of the `value` last written by Terraform, managed by the provider.
A different checksum, or none (resource imported, secret modified outside of Terraform) plans an update of the secret.
Beware that the checksum of a short or guessable value can be brute-forced.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Secret can be imported by specifying the instance's unique identifier.
# Its value is unknown to Terraform: the first apply writes the configured one.
terraform import aria_secret.example e74522bd-8adf-4bc4-ab5d-a2ffe9048d52
```
